clauses.short: Vesting program that escrows tokens against a schedule
clauses.text: Implement a vesting program on LEZ that locks tokens in escrow against a configured schedule. The program must support:
clauses.note: Native LEZ and token schedules. Each schedule's tokens sit in a program-derived escrow (one per schedule, or one shared per batch) that only the program debits, with its PDA seed (DECISIONS D-07, D-13).

clauses.short: Cliff + linear vesting
clauses.text: Cliff + linear vesting: tokens become claimable in a lump sum at the cliff date, then linearly over the remaining duration (e.g., 1-year cliff, 3-year linear release).
clauses.note: The lump sum is the creator's `cliff_amount`, released at `cliff_ts`; the rest vests linearly to `end_ts` (hand-computed values before, at and after the cliff, in the tail and at the end, plus property tests). The guest runs the same `escapement-core` function; in-process tests show the cliff payment and the pre-cliff refusal. The sequencer suite runs linear and milestone schedules, not a cliff.

clauses.short: Fully linear vesting
clauses.text: Fully linear vesting: no cliff; tokens accrue continuously from the start date.

clauses.short: Milestone vesting, fixed amount per signal
clauses.text: Milestone-based vesting: the schedule creator explicitly signals completion of discrete tranches; each signal unlocks a fixed token amount for the beneficiary to claim.
clauses.note: The creator signals and the beneficiary then claims exactly that tranche (3,000 of 10,000) in `negative_guards_*`; the stateful suite has the creator signal among its random operations. When a milestone authority is named at creation it replaces the creator exclusively (SR2, DECISIONS D-06): `full_lifecycle_*` and the sequencer suite signal through such an authority.

clauses.short: Beneficiary set at creation
clauses.text: The schedule creator specifies the beneficiary at schedule creation.

clauses.short: Claim to a public or a private account
clauses.text: Recipients can claim vested tokens to a public account or to a private account.
clauses.note: Native and token claims, public and private, on the sequencer; the private ones also with real RISC Zero proofs verified by the sequencer (EVIDENCE E-13). The in-process real-proof test runs in CI's manual job only.

clauses.short: Creator does not learn the private account
clauses.text: The schedule creator does not learn the recipient's private account address from the claim interaction.
clauses.note: No private account id, nullifier key or viewing key in the transaction bytes, events or state; fresh aliases, nullifiers and commitments per claim. The claims themselves stay linkable through the public beneficiary, schedule, amount and time, as the RFP's privacy limitation accepts.

clauses.short: Cancelable set at creation, default cancelable
clauses.text: The schedule creator sets whether the schedule is cancelable at creation time (default: cancelable).
clauses.note: The SDK's requests default to cancelable; the CLI's `create` is cancelable unless `--non-cancelable` is given (the suite creates its linear schedule without the flag and cancels it).

clauses.short: One-way conversion to non-cancelable
clauses.text: A cancelable schedule can be converted to non-cancelable by the creator; this conversion is irreversible.
clauses.note: No message makes a schedule cancelable again. When a cancel authority was named at creation, that authority (not the creator) converts, as it alone cancels (DECISIONS D-06).

clauses.short: Cancel returns the unvested balance to the creator
clauses.text: When a cancelable schedule is cancelled, the unclaimed, unvested token balance returns to the creator's account.
clauses.code_says: The refund goes to the schedule's `refund_holding`, which the creator may set at creation to any valid account, not only its own: `full_lifecycle_*` refunds 40,000 to a treasury distinct from the creator (DECISIONS D-06, D-13). Refunds go to the creator's account by default (SDK and CLI) and in every other test.
clauses.remaining: Restricting `refund_holding` to the creator's own account, or the RFP accepting a creator-named refund account; changing it changes the guest's image id.

clauses.short: Vested tokens stay claimable after cancel
clauses.text: Tokens already vested but not yet claimed remain claimable by the beneficiary after cancellation.

clauses.short: Transferability set at creation, immutable
clauses.text: The schedule creator can configure whether the vesting position (beneficiary rights) is transferable to a new beneficiary. Transferability must be set at schedule creation and cannot be changed afterwards.
clauses.note: A transfer of a non-transferable schedule exits with code 21. The stateful suite asserts after every random step (transfers, claims, cancels, make-non-cancelable, refused probes) that each schedule's `transferable` equals the value it was created with; the IDL test pins the program's complete message set, none of which sets the flag.

clauses.short: Batch creation; maximum per transaction documented
clauses.text: Multi-recipient batch creation: a creator can set up vesting schedules for multiple recipients in a single operation, up to the LEZ transaction size limit. Document the maximum number of recipients achievable in one transaction.
clauses.note: N_max measured on LEZ v0.4.0-rc3 for three schedule shapes and both assets, N_max + 1 refused (OutOfGas): docs/gas-and-batch.md. Re-measured on testnet 0.4 in M4.

clauses.short: An event per state transition; schema documented
clauses.text: The program emits a log event (using the LEZ event/log mechanism; see LP-0012) for each state transition: schedule creation, claim, cancellation, milestone signal, and beneficiary transfer. Event schema must be documented.
clauses.remaining: Reading the events back through an indexer: on LEZ v0.4.0-rc3 `getEvents` is the indexer's RPC, not the sequencer's, so this waits on LEZ testnet 0.4 (M4).
clauses.note: All eight events asserted in-process, including the `Claimed` event of a private claim; selectors checked; schema in docs/events.md and the IDL.

clauses.short: SDK for Logos modules: full lifecycle, public and private claims
clauses.text: Provide an SDK that can be used to build Logos modules interacting with the vesting program. The SDK must expose the full lifecycle: create schedule, query claimable amount, claim, cancel, signal milestone, and transfer beneficiary. The SDK must support claiming to both public and private accounts.
clauses.remaining: The module has no signal-milestone, transfer-beneficiary or private-claim method yet and creates linear and cliff schedules only; the mini-app's and module's tests are not in CI yet, since the module's workspace needs the Logos Rust SDK source that `nix build` fetches, and the view's tests need Qt (`qmltestrunner`).
clauses.note: The Rust SDK has builders for every operation and both assets, and every step of the sequencer suite goes through it. `escapement_core_module` (basecamp/) wraps it as a Logos Core module: configure, schedules (claimable now, next unlock), prepare_create (linear, cliff), prepare_claim (public), prepare_cancel, approve and reject; it ran in headless Logos Core (31 of 31 steps) and under Basecamp 0.4.0-rc.2, both on a local v0.4.0-rc3 sequencer.

clauses.short: CLI: create, claim, cancel, signal, query claimable
clauses.text: Provide a CLI that covers core functionality of the program. The CLI may have fewer features than the GUI mini-app but must support all essential operations: create schedule, claim, cancel, signal milestone, and query claimable amount.
clauses.remaining: Remote endpoints and wallet-held keys for LEZ testnet 0.4 (M4).
clauses.note: On a local sequencer the CLI creates, claims (public, and private into the beneficiary's own private account), cancels, signals and shows a schedule (`show`: claimable now and the next unlock), for native and token schedules. The suite reads `show` for the cancel record; it does not assert its `claimable_now` field.

clauses.short: Private path: gas check with an actionable error
clauses.text: When using the private account path, it must confirm that the beneficiary account has sufficient gas to cover the claim; a clear, actionable error must be shown if the balance is insufficient.
clauses.remaining: The mini-app has no private claim yet (public claims only); a separate private fee-payer account (M2).
clauses.note: The SDK refuses an under-funded private payer with the shortfall; the CLI checks the private account's balance against the exact fee reserve before proving, and the suite checks each balance after equals the credit less that reserve.

clauses.short: Privacy disclosure before each private claim
clauses.text: When using the private account path, the mini-app must display a privacy disclosure before each claim, identifying what will be visible on-chain (claim amount, beneficiary address, vesting schedule address) and what will not be traceable (the destination private account and subsequent movements).
clauses.remaining: The mini-app has no private claim yet (public claims only), so no disclosure screen (M3).
clauses.note: The SDK's disclosure (PR 235's wording) is bound to a confirmation token for the exact claim; the CLI prints it with its token and sends only with `--confirm <token>`; a wrong token is refused before anything is proven.

clauses.short: Atomic claim; retry without loss
clauses.text: A claim is atomic: a failed or rejected claim does not consume vested tokens and leaves the claimant able to retry without loss.
clauses.note: Refused claims leave the state byte-identical and a later claim succeeds; a raced or stale proven private claim rolls back whole and is retried in one transaction.

clauses.short: Atomic cancellation
clauses.text: A schedule cancellation is atomic: partial failure leaves the schedule in its prior state, not an undefined one.
clauses.note: `c1_*` cancels a fully claimed schedule: `Cancel` first sets the schedule to wait for the clock reply, then the continuation refuses (code 20); the test compares every account before and after and finds the schedule back in its prior, uncancelled state. The other tests compare the whole state after cancels refused at the first step (wrong authority, cancelled twice, after non-cancelable, by the beneficiary).

clauses.short: Concurrent claims on independent schedules
clauses.text: Concurrent claims against independent schedules must not corrupt shared program state.
clauses.note: Interleaved claims, including schedules that share a batch escrow and a claim and a cancel in the same block, with per-escrow and global supply conserved after every step.

clauses.short: Milestone signal idempotent, deterministic error
clauses.text: Milestone signalling is idempotent per milestone index: signalling the same milestone twice must be rejected with a deterministic error and must not double-unlock tokens.
clauses.note: A second signal of the same index exits with code 25 and the schedule stays byte-identical.

clauses.short: One claim, one transaction
clauses.text: A single claim completes within one LEZ transaction.

proposal.as_filed: public: native + token; private: native and token with real proofs on the sequencer, one transaction per claim once the private token holding exists

clauses.code_says: A claim into a private account that has no holding of the token yet takes two transactions: one private `InitializeHolding`, then the claim (E2E `private-token-holding` before `claim-private-token-*`); a claim without the holding is refused. Public claims, native private claims and token private claims into an existing holding take one transaction each.
clauses.remaining: Folding the private holding's initialization into the claim, so a fresh private token account also claims in one transaction (M2).

clauses.short: Mini-app and SDK: public and private claims
clauses.text: The mini-app and SDK must support claiming to both public and private accounts.
clauses.remaining: Private claims from the mini-app (it claims to public accounts only, M3).
clauses.note: The SDK (and the CLI through it) claims to public accounts and into the beneficiary's own private account.

clauses.short: Mini-app disclosure before each private claim
clauses.text: When using the private account path, the mini-app must display the pre-confirmation privacy disclosure described in the Usability section before each claim, identifying what is visible on-chain (claim amount, beneficiary address, vesting schedule address) and what remains private (the destination private account and subsequent movements of claimed tokens).
clauses.remaining: The mini-app has no private claim yet, so no disclosure screen (M3).
clauses.note: As U5: the SDK's disclosure names these items and is bound to a confirmation token; the CLI shows it and sends only with that token.

clauses.short: SDK refuses a non-private target on the private path
clauses.text: When using the private account path, the SDK must validate that the claim target is a private (shielded) account before submitting the transaction, and reject with an explicit error if it is not.
clauses.note: The CLI runs the same check on its key file's account before building anything.

clauses.short: Separate cancellation authority
clauses.text: The creator can nominate a separate cancellation authority distinct from the creator wallet (useful when vesting is managed by a multisig or DAO).
clauses.note: The authority replaces the creator exclusively for cancel and make-non-cancelable; a multisig or DAO program acts as its own PDA (`AsPda`), and a program the user merely signs for cannot act in the user's name (code 35).

clauses.short: Separate milestone authority that excludes the creator
clauses.text: The creator can nominate a separate milestone authority distinct from the creator wallet. Creator-controlled milestone authority is appropriate for team vesting, but creates a conflict of interest when vesting is used for buyer protection (e.g., creator collateral vesting from a token launch per RFP-015 or RFP-016): the creator could approve milestones and drain funds immediately. Delegating milestone authority to a governance body or multisig that excludes the creator prevents this.
clauses.note: With a milestone authority named, the creator's own signal is refused (code 13), in-process and on the sequencer.

clauses.short: Who pays
clauses.text: Who pays: whether fees (if any) are charged to the schedule creator, the beneficiary at claim time, or both.
clauses.note: The creator only; the beneficiary pays no protocol fee at claim.

clauses.short: When fees are collected
clauses.text: When fees are collected: at schedule creation, at each claim event, at cancellation, or a combination.
clauses.note: At creation only (single and batch).

clauses.short: Fee rate and fee switch
clauses.text: Fee rate: the exact rate or range, including whether a governance-activatable fee switch is included for future adjustment.
clauses.note: 0 bps at launch, switchable by the admin authority (`lez-admin-authority` v0.2.0) up to an immutable 100 bps cap; an optional broker fee up to 500 bps.

clauses.short: Where fees are routed
clauses.text: Where fees are routed: the destination account or mechanism (protocol treasury, burn, staking reward pool, etc.).
clauses.note: Into a fee vault per asset (a LEZ holding carries one token), withdrawn by the treasury; this keeps working after the admin renounces.

clauses.short: Batch size bound documented
clauses.text: The batch size is bounded by the LEZ transaction size limit, which the implementation must document.
clauses.note: The binding limit on LEZ v0.4.0-rc3 is gas, not bytes: docs/gas-and-batch.md gives N_max per shape and asset, and N_max + 1 is refused with OutOfGas.
